data.title: Fair Isaac Corporation stock trades up, here is why
data.description:
What happened?

Shares of credit scoring and analytics company FICO jumped 5.9% in the morning session after the company announced an agreement with Xactus to make its Preferred Program available to all mortgage industry clients.

The company said in a press release that the agreement also extends access to mortgage credit reseller clients served through the XedaLink and SharperLending platforms. Through the monthly FICO Preferred Program, participating lenders can access the Classic FICO Score and FICO Score 10T for a $10 wholesale price per bureau, per borrower, for the bundled scores, the release showed. The release also noted that the FICO wholesale price is unchanged for 2027.

What is the market telling us

Fair Isaac Corporation’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 35 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.

The previous big move we wrote about was 25 days ago when the stock dropped 7.5% on the news that Wells Fargo downgraded the company to Equal Weight alongside price target reductions from UBS and BMO Capital Markets. Wells Fargo analyst Jason Haas downgraded the stock from Overweight and reduced his target to $735 from $800, while UBS trimmed its price target to $942 from $1,100, per reporting from Investing.com and StreetInsider. BMO Capital lowered its target to $897 and cut its fiscal 2027 earnings forecast to $44.87 per share. All three brokerages responded to Fair Isaac's newly announced Preferred Program, which bundles the Classic FICO Score and FICO Score 10T at a $10 wholesale price for lenders committing to pull FICO on all mortgage applications.

The revisions reflect Wall Street concerns that Fair Isaac is conceding pricing power to defend volume as rival model VantageScore 4.0 advances under updated Federal Housing Finance Agency guidelines. Haas noted in research detailed by TipRanks that widespread lender enrollment in the fixed-fee tier eliminates expected 2027 price increases.

Fair Isaac Corporation is down 56.1% since the beginning of the year, and at $721.14 per share, it is trading 60.9% below its 52-week high of $1,845 from December 2025. Despite the year-to-date decline, investors who bought $1,000 worth of Fair Isaac Corporation’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,036.

data.title: Danaher Partners With Microsoft For AI-powered Ecosystem Involving Scientific Instruments
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - On Friday, Danaher Corp. (DHR) announced a strategic partnership with Microsoft Corp. (MSFT) to develop smart scientific instruments and an interoperable AI-powered ecosystem connecting Danaher technologies with the wider laboratory industry. The partnership aims to streamline scientific workflows and help researchers turn scientific questions into experimental results and insights more quickly.

Danaher and Microsoft are developing a shared AI platform using Microsoft Azure and Microsoft Foundry to control scientific instruments, analyze results and improve laboratory workflows.

The first commercial application, including MetaXpress Acquire AI Assistant, will launch this year, with additional AI-powered instruments planned for 2027.

As per the terms of the partnership, Danaher and Microsoft are developing AI-powered instruments to help scientists plan experiments, control equipment, analyze results, identify issues and recommend next steps.

In preliminary tests, novice scientists using an AI assistant on a Leica microscope completed experiments up to 83% faster and with 68% fewer steps than those working without AI.

On the NYSE, the shares for Danaher are trading 1.12 percent down at $225.01.

On Nasdaq, the shares for Microsoft are trading 0.56 percent down at $501.07.

data.title: Wagyu’s XMR1 wrapped Monero plunges 99% after $13 million hack as founder promises refunds
data.description:
Cross-chain swap and bridge platform Wagyu's wrapped Monero token XMR1 collapsed more than 99% on Friday after an attacker allegedly accessed its deployer wallet and dumped the stolen tokens on Hyperliquid.

XMR1 fell from nearly $500 to as low as $0.65. Blockchain tracker Lookonchain first reported that an attacker received 5.2 million XMR1 from the token's deployer wallet and sold a portion of them for USDC on Hyperliquid before using those funds to buy nearly 7,500 ETH.

The token is a wrapped version of Monero that can be used and redeemed on the Wagyu platform. Monero's actual XMR is unaffected by this incident.

The platform's pseudonymous founder, who goes by the moniker PerpetualCow, blamed the hack on a breach at the Icelandic hosting provider 1984.hosting, saying the XMR1 deployer key had been exposed.

"The XMR1 deployer key was held on an OLD server on there that I DELETED, but somehow the logs/files were still kept," Cow wrote on X.

PerpetualCow.hl
@PerpetualCow

Post-mortem of the $13m XMR hack: It's WORSE than I thought. Turns out that the entire hosting provider of https://t.co/aZzKk23eCg got hacked with everyone's data + internal server files today. The XMR1 deployer key was held on an OLD server on there that I DELETED, but somehow the logs/files were still kept. Lesson to learn here is that these hosting providers keep your data/logs even after you delete your server with them. Like I said before, everyone who lost money due to this will be refunded by me personally and Wagyu will re-launch at a later stage. Give me some time please.

Nov 20, 2026

Icelandic outlets DV and mbl.is reported on Friday that 1984 temporarily suspended its services following a cyberattack. However, this does not automatically confirm the founder's claims about bad actors accessing the retained keys.

Wagyu's website displayed a notice saying the service was "temporarily unavailable" at the time of publication.

"Everyone who lost money due to this will be refunded by me personally and Wagyu will re-launch at a later stage," PerpetualCow said in his post. He did not provide a timetable.

data.title: MU, SNDK, Other Chipmakers Plunge Amid AI Trade Weakness — UBS Says Risk-Reward In Equities Has Become ‘More Balanced’
data.description:
Key points:
  • UBS expects 25-basis-point Fed rate hikes in December and March but does not anticipate a prolonged tightening cycle.
  • It said AI model and application revenues would likely need to reach at least $1.5 trillion by 2030 for an adequate return.
  • UBS remains cautious on leveraged capacity providers and lower-quality suppliers.

Micron Technology (MU), SanDisk (SNDK) and other chipmakers’ shares plunged in early Friday trading as sentiment remained under pressure amid a continuing selloff in technology and artificial intelligence (AI) stocks.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq plunged over 2%, while the S&P 500 index fell around 1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average, meanwhile, traded marginally higher, boosted by gains in healthcare and retail stocks.

UBS said in its Friday note that recent selling followed persistent pressure on chipmakers and cloud companies as investors questioned the scale of investment needed to build AI infrastructure. The “risk-reward in equities had become more balanced”, it noted.

Higher Rate Expectations Add To Pressure

UBS said that monetary policy uncertainty “added to fragile market sentiment”. The minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting indicated that nearly all policymakers expected further tightening if the U.S. economy developed as anticipated.

The firm expects 25-basis-point rate increases in December 2026 and March 2027, but does not anticipate a prolonged tightening cycle. “The cumulative effects of higher rates look set to weigh on consumer demand, while we believe base effects will contribute to a moderation in underlying inflation,” it said.

UBS also said market sentiment was dented by a Hunterbrook short-seller report raising concerns about AMD's business ties to China amid tighter U.S. chip restrictions, as well as Nvidia's continued stock decline despite an upbeat revenue forecast earlier in the week.

An AMD spokesperson told Bloomberg that the company “complies with applicable US export control laws and regulations and maintains rigorous processes to ensure compliance across our global operations.”

AI Investment Story Remains Intact

The market selloff extended to semiconductor ETFs, with the iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX), VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH), and the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) declining up to 7%. Sentiment around all three tickers remained ‘bearish’ on Stocktwits.

However, according to UBS, the AI story remained intact. “We do not think that the economic expansion, corporate earnings cycle, or structural AI investment story has broken,” it said.

The firm expects economic growth close to trend in 2027, rising corporate profits, further growth in AI investment, and moderating inflation later in the year.

UBS estimates cumulative U.S. technology investment in AI infrastructure could approach $5 trillion by the end of 2028. It said AI model and application revenues would likely need to reach at least $1.5 trillion by 2030 for the industry to earn an adequate return.

“Competition, price cuts, costly monetization, and open-weight models may threaten returns. Financing, regulatory, and company-specific risks also add to uncertainty,” UBS said.

UBS Sees Equity Gains In 2027

In its base case, UBS expects approximately 15% S&P 500 earnings growth in 2027 and sees further upside for equities, although it cautioned that the range of potential outcomes has widened.

“The challenge for investors in 2027 is constructing portfolios that can prove resilient across a variety of scenarios,” UBS said.

Within U.S. technology, the firm favors financially strong hyperscalers with visible AI monetization, alongside select leaders in compute, foundries, semiconductor equipment and infrastructure software.

“We remain cautious on leveraged capacity providers, lower-quality suppliers, and companies whose valuations depend on persistent bottlenecks or distant cash flows,” UBS said.

Where UBS Sees Opportunity

The firm noted that elevated yields offer an attractive combination of income and potential portfolio resilience, while providing a return cushion even if rates do not decline materially. It sees “attractive return opportunities in quality bonds”.

Within fixed income, UBS sees the “best return opportunity” in emerging market and high-yield bonds.

data.title: Carnival Orders Two New Cruise Ships From Italy's Fincantieri for Over $3 Billion — Update
data.description:
By Mauro Orru

Carnival has placed an order for two new cruise ships from Italy's Fincantieri, moving to expand its fleet as demand from travelers remains strong.

The Italian shipbuilder said it had signed a contract with the cruise operator for the design and construction of the vessels that will have roughly 1,650 guest cabins each and will use LNG as their primary fuel. A person familiar with the deal said the contract was valued at 3 billion euros ($3.29 billion).

Carnival Chief Executive Josh Weinstein said the group had 12 new ships on order for delivery through 2039 across Carnival Cruise Line, Princess and AIDA, giving Carnival flexibility to expand the choices and destinations it has on offer. The group has a fleet of more than 90 ships, according to its website.

In September, Carnival reported higher profit and revenue for the third quarter. Weinstein said at the time that booking trends had continued to strengthen throughout the quarter, with volumes meaningfully ahead of last year and far outpacing capacity growth.

Fincantieri said it would build the two ships for Carnival Cruise Line at its Marghera shipyard in north-eastern Italy, with deliveries scheduled in 2033 and 2035.

For Fincantieri, the order expands a decadeslong relationship with Carnival. Fincantieri has delivered 76 ships across Carnival's cruise line portfolio over the course of their 30-year relationship, including 15 for Carnival Cruise Line.

Write to Mauro Orru at mauro.orru@wsj.com

data.title: Broker tips: Ithaca Energy, Sage, Barclays
data.description:
Berenberg updated its model on Ithaca to incorporate Wednesday's Q3 numbers and other modelling changes, noting it remained positive on the group given its "strong operational delivery, organic growth outlook and attractive distributions".

The German bank highlighted record quarterly EBITDAX generation of $663m, which lifted year-to-date EBITDAX 20% to $1.8bn, alongside narrowed full-year production guidance of 123,000 to 127,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day. It also pointed to upgraded shareholder returns, with Ithaca now expecting to declare a total 2026 dividend of $560m to $580m, up 10% at the mid-point on prior guidance.

Berenberg added that Ithaca's $860m acquisition of Suncor assets offshore Canada - which was on track to complete in the first half of 2027 - was likely to drive upside to medium-term consensus forecasts and underpin an increased production outlook of 140,000 to 150,000 barrels of oil per day. Meanwhile, the Rosebank project remains on schedule for first oil in H127, pending regulatory approval expected by year-end.

Analysts at Canaccord Genuity lowered their target price on software firm Sage from 1,230p to 1,200p on Friday, pointing to a lack of near-term catalysts and an elevated valuation.

Canaccord Genuity noted that its recent downgrade to 'hold' was predicated on the stock's strong run off "SaaS-pocalypse" lows, fair valuation, and limited upside to consensus, adding that FY26 results delivered along those exact lines.

While FY26 revenues of £2.78bn came in 1% ahead of forecasts with 10.3% organic growth, and adjusted underlying earnings rose 14% to £683m, the Canadian bank highlighted a stark divergence in performance. Sage's mid-market ERP platform Intacct remained the primary growth engine with over 20% expansion, outpacing Oracle's Netsuite, whereas its core SME software offering grew at a "relatively pedestrian" 5% to 6%, implying market share losses to rivals Xero and Intuit.

Canaccord nudged its forecasts up by 2% to 3% following FY27 organic growth guidance of roughly 10%. However, it warned that near-term operating leverage will be muted by ongoing AI and system investments, and noted a new share buyback will likely have to wait until the second half due to leverage.

"While visibility here is good we see a lack of catalysts - growth is guided a touch ahead of pre-results consensus, but a margin beat seems unlikely due to investments," said Canaccord, which reiterated its 'hold' rating. "With the stock's 13x EV/EBITDA and 18x P/E multiples at the high end of the global peer group, we maintain Hold with a tweaked £12 target."

Shore Capital has questioned the strategic rationale behind a rumoured takeover of Metro Bank by Barclays, arguing that the deal would offer limited opportunities for cost savings and that rival lender Shawbrook could represent a more attractive acquisition target.

The broker's comments follow a Bloomberg report that Barclays was among several parties showing early interest in Metro Bank, alongside private equity firms Lone Star and Centerbridge, after the challenger bank put itself up for sale.

In a research note on Friday, Shore Capital said Barclays was a credible potential buyer, having previously acquired Tesco Bank and specialist mortgage lender Kensington, while reportedly also bidding for TSB. However, it argued that those acquisitions offered clearer strategic benefits, while the strategic logic for acquiring Metro Bank was considerably weaker, particularly given its existing access to relatively cheap funding.

Metro Bank's funding advantage was also supported by its expensive branch network, meaning widespread closures could undermine its deposit base while potentially incurring substantial lease-exit costs. Meanwhile, Barclays already had significant funding capacity, with third-quarter loan-to-deposit ratios of 92% in Barclays UK and 38% in its UK Corporate Bank division. Shore Capital said Metro Bank's surplus deposits would therefore offer limited immediate benefits, while opportunities for other cost savings appeared relatively modest.

Instead, Shore Capital suggested that Shawbrook could offer a better route for Barclays to expand its small and medium-sized business lending operations, offering greater potential funding synergies without the complications of a large branch network, while also trading at a more attractive valuation. Based on consensus forecasts for 2027, Shawbrook traded at 0.7 times tangible net asset value and five times earnings, compared with 1.1 times and eight times respectively for Metro Bank.

Shore Capital retained its 'buy' recommendation on Barclays with a 560p target price, implying around 40% upside from the 401p share price referenced in its note.

data.title: Latam stocks tumble to one-year low, FX falls on rate worries
data.description:
Key points:
  • Markets await Lula's pick for finance minister
  • BofA sees scope for renewed capital inflows into Brazil
  • Mexican retail sales signal softer domestic demand

By Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Latin American equities fell to over one-year lows on Friday as a global equity selloff intensified after Anthropic's IPO failed to restore confidence in the AI sector, while prospects of higher US interest rates kept pressure on regional currencies.

While Latin American markets have limited direct exposure to the technology sector, the deterioration in global risk sentiment spilled over into the region.

MSCI's index of Latin American equities (.MILA00000PUS) fell 0.86% and was on track for its lowest weekly decline since November 2025, while the corresponding currency gauge (.MILA00000CUS) fell 1.5% and was on track for its fourth consecutive weekly loss.

Brazil's benchmark Bovespa index (.BSVP), which accounts for the largest weighting in the MSCI Latin America index, fell 0.69%, pressured by losses in heavyweight energy stocks.

Investor also monitored domestic developments. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is nearing a decision on his next finance minister, with an announcement possible as early as next week, according to six sources familiar with the discussions.

The Brazilian real was down 0.24% against the US dollar.

"Gains in the Brazilian real were only fleeting, with investors still wary that President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva has no interest in fiscal consolidation," said Chris Turner, global head of markets research at ING.​‌

Separately, Bank of America said there remains a potential path for capital inflows to return to Latin America's largest economy despite a challenging economic environment at home and abroad.

MEXICO TRADE HOPES RISE; COMMODITIES RETREAT

In Mexico, the peso was up 0.29%. Investors took note of a potentially positive development on the trade front as EU agriculture commissioner Christophe Hansen said he expects Mexico to clear the final hurdle for a new EU trade pact to take effect by the end of the year, bringing Mexican and European interests closer together.

Meanwhile, Mexican retail sales fell in September from the previous month, data from the national statistics agency showed, pointing to softer consumer demand despite remaining higher than a year ago.

Broader global factors also weighed on sentiment. Commodity prices fell, with gold down 2% and copper was headed for its biggest weekly drop in 19 months.

Chile's peso fell 0.29% against the dollar, while Peru's sol slipped 0.15%.​‌

Brent crude fell around 1% as concerns over supply disruptions eased, with exports from the Middle East remaining resilient despite Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's capital, Riyadh, and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

Separately, Polish central banker Joanna Tyrowicz told PAP News Agency that interest rates should be "much higher" and that the central bank's communication should remain "hawkish".​‌

data.title: Consumer expectations enjoy post-election boost - UMich
data.description:
Key points:
  • All major US indexes lower, Nasdaq off ~2.5%
  • Tech biggest laggard among S&P 500 sectors; Cons staples up most
  • STOXX 600 index slides >1.8%
  • Dollar falls; gold, bitcoin down >3%; US crude off ~1%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield falls to ~4.95%

CONSUMER EXPECTATIONS ENJOY POST-ELECTION BOOST - UMICH

The University of Michigan's (UMich) second and final stab at November consumer sentiment (USUMSF=ECI) showed the mood among consumers wasn't quite as morose as originally reported.

The index came in at 51.5, as analysts expected, a slight improvement over its initial 51.0 reading.

With this, the sentiment of the American consumer, whose spending accounts for about 70% of the US economy, has grown about 6.5% sunnier compared with October's final reading.

Less encouraging was the survey participants' assessment of present conditions, which was revised 3.1% lower. But a 3.9% upward revision to near-term expectations made up for that. Both metrics showed monthly improvements of 5.8% and 8.4%, respectively.

The improvements were "led by substantial post-election gains in both short- and long-run expected business conditions," writes Joanne Hsu, UMich's director of consumer surveys. "Current personal finances improved for low-wealth consumers and, to a lesser extent, middle-wealth consumers, who experienced some relief with falling gas prices."

"Those with the largest stockholdings reported a decline in personal finances, consistent with continued AI-related agitation in stock markets," Hsu adds.

The graphic below shows consumer expectations currently sit 19.7% below the initial pandemic-related shutdown shock.

The inflation expectations element showed respondents now expect annual price growth of 3.7% a year from now. That's significantly cooler than UMich's originally reported 4.3% take for the current month, and marks a full percentage point drop from the final October print.

But it's still 1.1 percentage points hotter than the most recent core CPI reading. Note: year-on-year CPI data was unavailable for October, due to a year-ago data gap related to the government shutdown.

Longer term, consumers expect annual inflation of 3.3% five years from now, down from 3.5% a month ago.

data.title: Apollo and Goldman Sachs Announce Pricing of $44 Billion SpaceX GPU Financing
data.description:
Transaction was led by Apollo and Goldman Sachs Alongside Leading Global Investors

NEW YORK, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Apollo and Goldman Sachs today announced the successful pricing of approximately $44 billion of senior and subordinated notes to fund the purchase of GPUs and related equipment for SpaceX . The transaction, which was oversubscribed and upsized as a result of strong investor demand, will deliver the next generation of NVIDIA Vera Rubin chips for SpaceX’s terrestrial compute buildout and represents the largest GPU financing executed to date. Lease schedules are expected to commence upon delivery of GPUs and related equipment in the first half of 2027.

Financing was committed by funds and affiliates managed by Apollo and Goldman Sachs, with funds and accounts managed by BlackRock, Goldman Sachs Asset Management and capital accounts advised by KKR providing anchor commitments in the transaction. Apollo Global Securities and Goldman Sachs served as Co-Global Coordinators, while Goldman Sachs served as Sole Structuring Agent.

“SpaceX is one of the most ambitious builders of compute in the world, and we are pleased to have led this financing alongside Goldman Sachs,” said Apollo Partner Jamshid Ehsani. “This transaction reflects the strength of Apollo’s integrated platform, where origination, structuring, syndication and principal investing work together to deliver flexible capital at scale. It also reflects our focus on downside-protected, asset-based structures.”

Apollo was advised by Morgan Stanley, Citi and PJT Partners on the transaction.

Latham & Watkins LLP served as legal counsel to Apollo. Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP served as investor counsel.

About Apollo

Apollo is a high-growth, global alternative asset manager. In our asset management business, we seek to provide our clients excess return at every point along the risk-reward spectrum from investment grade credit to private equity. For more than three decades, our investing expertise across our fully integrated platform has served the financial return needs of our clients and provided businesses with innovative capital solutions for growth. Through Athene, our retirement services business, we specialize in helping clients achieve financial security by providing a suite of retirement savings products and acting as a solutions provider to institutions. Our patient, creative, and knowledgeable approach to investing aligns our clients, businesses we invest in, our employees, and the communities we impact, to expand opportunity and achieve positive outcomes. data.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Today: Glassnode Warns of Holder Losses as BTC Approaches Critical $61K Support
data.description:
Glassnode data also points to a shrinking profit margin for the average Bitcoin holder, raising concerns that another decline could push the market into an unrealized-loss phase.

Fundamental Analysis

Bitcoin faced several sources of selling pressure during the November 17–19 period. US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded combined net outflows of approximately $1.13 billion, suggesting that institutional demand weakened as market conditions deteriorated. Expectations of a tighter Federal Reserve stance and weakness across technology stocks added to the cautious mood surrounding risk assets.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

Derivatives activity further intensified the decline. CoinGlass recorded approximately $201.51 million in Bitcoin derivatives liquidations over the preceding 24 hours. Long positions accounted for $167.97 million, compared with $33.55 million in short liquidations. The imbalance indicates that traders positioned for higher prices absorbed most of the losses as BTC continued to fall.

The average funding rate also turned slightly negative, reflecting a shift in derivatives positioning. However, the liquidation figures do not yet establish that the market has reached a capitulation phase. Instead, they show that bullish positions faced greater pressure during the latest decline.

Liquidity conditions provide another concern. The shrinking supply of stablecoins points to a weaker pool of available capital across the crypto market. With ETF withdrawals accelerating and liquidity declining, Bitcoin may struggle to sustain a recovery without renewed spot demand.

Glassnode Highlights a Narrow Profit Margin

On-chain data from Glassnode shows that Bitcoin remains above its realized price, meaning the average holder is still marginally in profit. However, the MVRV ratio, which compares Bitcoin's market value with its realized value, has moved close to the breakeven level of 1.

The chart highlights MVRV hovering near breakeven 509 days before the projected April 2028 Bitcoin halving, mirroring patterns observed in previous pre-halving cycles. Source: Glassnode via X

The reading is particularly significant because it suggests that the average investor has limited unrealized gains to absorb further price declines. As of November 2026, the MVRV ratio was only slightly above 1, leaving holders increasingly exposed to a move below their aggregate cost basis.

A fall beneath that threshold would place the average Bitcoin holder in an unrealized-loss position for the first time since early 2023. Such a shift could increase selling pressure, particularly if investors decide to reduce exposure rather than wait for a potential recovery.

Glassnode's historical comparison also places the current reading approximately 509 days before the estimated April 2028 Bitcoin halving. Previous market cycles experienced periods when MVRV approached breakeven levels ahead of their respective halvings. However, the indicator alone does not establish whether the current market will follow the same pattern.

Technical Analysis

Bitcoin's technical structure remains firmly bearish despite signs that the market may be approaching an oversold condition. TradingView's Bitstamp feed placed BTCUSD near $61,368 in the latest available snapshot, representing a decline of approximately $2,396, or 3.76%.

BTCUSD has reached the lower boundary of a previous support zone, with oversold RSI and an extended gap from the EMA stack indicating potential for a modest rebound. Source: KrisadaYoonaisil on TradingView

The aggregated showed 14 sell signals, nine neutral readings and only three buy signals. Moving averages accounted for most of the negative readings, with 13 sell signals against one neutral and one buy. This configuration reflects the extent of the recent decline and confirms that the BTC price remains below its major trend indicators.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stood at 20, placing it deep in oversold territory. The Stochastic indicator also dropped to 3, while the Williams Percent Range reached -99. These readings suggest that selling has become unusually intense over the short term.

Other indicators present a mixed picture. The Commodity Channel Index (CCI) generated a buy signal at -117, while Momentum also indicated a possible rebound. However, the MACD remained bearish at -4,596, and the Average Directional Index (ADX) stood at 43, indicating that the prevailing trend remains strong.

The moving-average structure reinforces the downside bias. The 10-day exponential moving average (EMA) was near $65,713, while the 20-day EMA stood around $69,611. Longer-term averages were also considerably higher than the current market price. This wide separation indicates that Bitcoin has experienced substantial downward momentum and would need sustained buying interest to reclaim those levels.

$61K Support Remains Critical

The immediate focus is on Bitcoin's ability to defend the $61,000 area, which coincides with a major daily demand zone identified in the TradingView analysis. The sharp bearish impulse has brought BTC close to this region, making its reaction there important for determining the next short-term move.

The deeply oversold indicators and the distance from the major moving averages leave room for a relief bounce. However, oversold conditions do not guarantee an immediate reversal, particularly when the broader trend remains negative.

According to eLs-Trading on TradingView, traders should avoid trying to identify the exact bottom and wait for confirmation before acting around the demand zone. The analysis states: "Never chase or predict the bottom. Always wait for clear confirmation signals to validate the zone before entering."

If Bitcoin stabilizes above $61,000, the first important upside reference is around $65,500. A recovery toward $69,000 would represent the next resistance test. A sustained move above that level could improve the technical structure, although the broader moving-average configuration would still require attention.

Conversely, a decisive break below $61,000 could expose the previous low near $57,700. The classic S3 pivot level around $58,181 provides another downside reference within the same broader price region.

For now, Bitcoin's near-term direction depends on whether buyers can defend the $61,000 support area and generate enough demand to counter continued selling. Improving ETF flows and stronger spot-market participation would provide clearer evidence of recovery. Without those developments, the combination of weak liquidity, negative market sentiment and bearish moving averages continues to leave the BTC price vulnerable to further declines.

data.title: Micron leads semiconductor and AI stocks down as SOX plunges 7%
data.description:
Semiconductor stocks fell hard during Friday market action, led by Micron Technology plunging 11%, and further evidenced by the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index dropping 7%.

Micron sank despite its CEO indicating earlier this week that supply would be tighter in 2027 and 2028 than it was this year.

AMD tumbled nearly 8%, Taiwan Semiconductor declined 6%, Marvell sank 8.5%, Nvidia dropped 6%, Arm dove nearly 9%, and Broadcom decreased 8%.

Broadcom was hit by a report Friday morning that revealed Google is cutting planned shipments of its Broadcom-designed AI chips for 2027 while increasing orders for chips designed by MediaTek.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq dipped 2.5% by late morning trading. The Nasdaq has declined 15% since October 6.

"The same rate pressure hurting semis today could ultimately help create the bottom," said BofA analyst Vivek Arya in a Friday investor report. "US cloud capex is running ~$1.2Tn annualized vs. ~$1.5tn+ expected in CY27. Holding spend near today's run-rate implies ~20% CY27 capex haircut (~30GW vs. ~40GW expected) and up to 35-40% downside to AI semi EPS. Higher rates raise WACC, weaken marginal project IRRs + make external financing more expensive, potentially forcing lower-return projects out of buildout. N-t capex reset would hurt, but could make the cycle healthier: less speculative capacity, more disciplined spending, an underwriteable earnings base."

BofA said they are waiting to see capital expenditure reductions before becoming more positive on the semiconductor and AI trade.

"Our historical work shows the SOX typically bottoms 2-6 mos. before fundas and subsequently rallies ~42% on avg. as est. cuts become understood," Arya added. "The signal we want is therefore not higher earnings ests. It is lower capex/EPS ests. that stop producing lower stock prices. Peak rates can establish the multiple floor; quantified capex and EPS cuts can establish the earnings floor … That, more than the eventual Fed cut or earnings trough, could mark the start of the next SOX upcycle."

Analog stocks were also falling on Friday. Texas Instruments and Analog Devices both sank 5%, Onsemi was down 5.3%, and STMicroelectronics slid 6.5%.

Neoclouds and networking stocks were also bleeding during Friday market action. Nebius plummeted nearly 10%, CoreWeave collapsed by 9.6%, and IREN tumbled 11%. IREN was downgraded to Strong Sell from Hold this week by Seeking Alpha's Quant system.

Coherent cratered by 11%, Lumentum slumped nearly 10%, and Ciena fell about 9%.

data.title: SDMC's Third Consecutive Year at Google's TV Summit, Showcasing Home Physical AI
data.description:
BANGKOK, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- At Google's 2026 TV Summit in Bangkok, SDMC (00901.HK) returned as an invited speaker for the third consecutive year, advancing its AI Home strategy under the theme "Building the Future of Home Physical AI with Google".

Building on Google's ecosystem and technologies, SDMC introduced an innovative product concept. We further advanced Edge AI innovation with Amlogic, delivered a joint presentation with Altice Labs on TV Centric Home Physical AI, and signed an MOU to establish an AI Home Joint Innovation Lab.

From Connected Homes to Home Physical AI

At this year's TV Summit, SDMC explored Home Physical AI—intelligence that senses household conditions, understands context, and acts in the physical environment.

We envision the TV and living room as the center of the Home AI Agent experience—a shared screen in a shared space where family members can interact with AI together.

To explore this vision and inspire next-generation home experiences, we showcased the Cedar Display Hub, a concept prototype that combines an Android TV streaming dock with a companion second screen. Demonstrations included AI recaps without interrupting playback, cross-screen family games, home-camera highlights on TV, and more.

Connecting Google and Edge AI Technologies

Android TV and Google TV underpin entertainment, while Cedar combines Gemma-based Edge AI with Gemini-powered cloud reasoning for context-aware assistance. SDMC integrates these capabilities across devices and software and participates in Google Cloud's Proactive Physical AI Acceleration Program.

With Amlogic, SDMC demonstrated Edge AI for personalized interaction and family memory management. The A311Y3-powered Display Hub uses voiceprint and facial recognition to distinguish family members; the S905D5-powered AI NAS Frame supports recognition, classification, and search of locally stored family photos.

Building AI Home Services for Operators

For operators, SDMC's AI Home portfolio builds on established TV and broadband services. Its AI Streaming Box brings AI-enhanced entertainment, whole-home control, and family security to the TV; Google TV Projector extends premium viewing; and AI Fiber Gateway provides Wi-Fi 8 and XGS-PON connectivity.

AI Operation adds proactive monitoring, unified device management, and closed-loop support, helping operators explore new service opportunities and deepen household engagement.

Advancing Joint Innovation & Commercial Validation

These opportunities were also central to SDMC's joint presentation with Altice Labs. SDMC explained how Home AI Agents complement personal assistants and how cloud-edge AI enables dual-screen family experiences. Altice Labs drew on Sophia, its upcoming MEO TV assistant, to discuss the shift from on-demand responses toward proactive assistance.

Under the MOU, SDMC and Altice Labs plan to establish the AI Home Joint Innovation Lab, combining SDMC's integration capabilities with Altice Labs' operator expertise to explore family assistance, home security, and whole-home control. Selected scenarios are planned for a field pilot in Portugal, with commercial validation targeted for 2027.

Together, these efforts aim to make Home Physical AI useful for families and viable for operators.

data.title: CNH Names Paul Dick, President, North America
data.description:
Key points:
  • Paul Dick appointed President, North America, effective Jan. 1, 2027
  • Scott Harris to retire from role after 20 years with CNH and serve as senior advisor in 2027

Paul Dick, President of North America CNH

Basildon, UK — November 20, 2026 — CNH Industrial N.V. today announced the appointment of Paul Dick as president, North America, effective Jan. 1, 2027. Dick will succeed Scott Harris, who is retiring next year after 20 distinguished years with the company.

Harris will serve as president, North America, through Dec. 31. Beginning Jan. 1, Dick will assume the role, and Harris will remain with CNH as a senior advisor in 2027 to support a smooth transition.

"Scott Harris has given CNH 20 remarkable years, and the North America business he leaves behind is stronger, more connected to our dealers and better positioned for the future because of him," said Gerrit Marx, Chief Executive Officer of CNH. "He has shaped our dealer network, mentored countless leaders and set a standard of integrity and customer focus that defines who we are in North America. On behalf of the entire CNH team, I thank Scott for his countless contributions and wish him every happiness in this next chapter. We are fortunate that Scott will stay on to ensure Paul and the team are set up for continued success."

"Paul Dick is the right leader for the next chapter of North America. He brings a rare combination of operational discipline, services and recurring revenue expertise, and an authentic, lifelong connection to the agricultural equipment our customers depend on. His track record of driving margin expansion while scaling digital and connected solutions aligns directly with our strategic priorities and our Path to 2030," Marx said.

"It has been the honor of my career to lead this team," Harris said. "The dealers, employees and customers who make up CNH's North America business are the best in the industry. I'm proud of what we've built together, and I will leave with complete confidence in Paul and in the future of this business."

Dick is a senior operating executive with more than two decades of leadership experience in complex industrial businesses. In his most recent role at Ingersoll Rand, he led a team responsible for sales to key accounts directly and through a wide distribution, direct and retail network spanning from consumer products to large professional systems. He has led major business integrations and digital transformation initiatives.

“I’ve had a lifelong connection to agriculture and a deep respect for the people who depend on this industry every day. That makes the opportunity to lead CNH North America especially meaningful to me,” Dick said. “I look forward to working with our teams and dealers to build on the strong foundation already in place, move quickly on opportunities for growth and deliver exceptional outcomes for our customers and our business.”

Dick holds a master’s degree in industrial management and a bachelor’s degree in industrial engineering technology from the University of Central Missouri.

***

About CNH

CNH serves and advances the people who feed and build a growing world.

We are an iron-and-tech company, engineering intelligence, automation, and precision into the machines that move the global economy. Our equipment operates in more than 160 geographies, supported by a global team of more than 34,000 people, including engineers, technologists, and industry experts.

Our brands — Case IH, New Holland, STEYR, CNH Tech (including the Raven precision technology platform), and CNH Capital — together generated $18.1B in revenue in 2025.

Building on a legacy of innovation dating back to 1842, CNH has achieved multiple milestones including the first mass-produced tractor, the first twin-rotor combine, and the first factory-integrated precision farming system. Today, we are engineering autonomous and predictive machines that will shape the future of food and infrastructure.

data.title: Bulls on a roll. Nifty hit 9-month high as Rupee logs best weekly rally in 5 weeks; Bond yields ease
data.description:
Indian markets capped another strong week on Friday, extending their winning streak to four consecutive weeks and pushing benchmark indices to their highest levels in nine months as robust foreign inflows powered gains across equities, bonds and the currency market.

The Nifty 50 closed at a nine-month high of 25,800.60, while the Sensex ended at 83,919.71, marking the benchmarks’ fourth consecutive week of gains. Banking stocks remained the market’s biggest driver, with the Bank Nifty hitting a fresh record high of 64,680.80 before settling at 64,635, up 2.49 per cent for the day and nearly 16 per cent so far this month.

“The banking sector was leading from the front this week and closed with a whopping weekly gain of 5.9 per cent,” said Nagaraj Shetti, Senior Technical Research Analyst at HDFC Securities.

Foreign portfolio investors continued to dominate flows, pumping over ₹1 lakh crore into Indian equities during November so far, helping markets shrug off concerns around global technology stocks and elevated US yields. Siddhartha Khemka, Head of Research at Motilal Oswal Financial Services, said improving earnings visibility and a strengthening rupee have reinforced India’s appeal among overseas investors.

Rupee roars

The rupee emerged as the week’s standout performer, posting its strongest weekly gain in five weeks. The currency appreciated 1.67 per cent, or 157 paise, against the US dollar during the week, closing at 92.67 compared with 94.24 levels seen at the start of the week. On Friday alone, it gained 62 paise from the previous close of 93.29, climbing to its strongest level in about seven months despite the Dollar Index hovering near a 20-month high.

“Sustained FII inflows and positive domestic market sentiment could keep the rupee on a firm trajectory,” said Jateen Trivedi, Vice President, Research Analyst at LKP Securities.

Kunal Sodhani, Head-Treasury at Shinhan Bank, said the rupee’s resilience reflected a combination of strong foreign inflows, softer crude oil prices and a reversal in global investment flows towards emerging markets. “To prevent excessive rupee appreciation, the RBI may intervene through dollar purchases or encourage oil marketing companies to source part of their dollar requirements from the open market,” he added.

Crude cools

Falling crude oil prices also strengthened sentiment across asset classes. Brent crude eased to around $90 a barrel during the week, improving India’s macroeconomic outlook by lowering concerns around imported inflation and the current account deficit.

The bond market also joined the rally. Government security yields softened as declining crude oil prices and easing US Treasury yields improved sentiment. The benchmark 6.94 per cent GS 2036 yield fell 6 basis points during the session to close at 7.19 per cent from 7.25 per cent previously, signalling continued demand for sovereign debt.

Lower oil prices, resilient domestic growth prospects and sustained foreign inflows have created a favourable backdrop for Indian assets, said experts. With equities at nine-month highs, the rupee at a seven-month peak and bond yields easing, investors will closely track upcoming US inflation data and month-end derivatives expiry for further cues on the direction of foreign flows.
